headline: Every pack of pitta checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
heroLede: Mr. Pitta makes pitta bread in packs like its 21 cm five-pack, now from its Campbellfield factory. Packs of different breads and sizes look alike on the line, so the seal, the label and the date are what keep each run right. This is what a camera check could look like at the end of a bread packing line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every bag is sealed straight across, with no crease and no bread caught in the seal. An open bag means stale bread and a complaint from the store.
labelLede: A white pack and a wholemeal pack can look much the same at line speed. The camera checks every pack carries the right label for the bread inside, straight and intact.
codeLede: The best-before and batch code has to be right and readable on every pack. The system reads the printed code and compares it with the product and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Film offcuts, glove pieces and loose parts can end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a crate.

vocab.alert: Four creased seals in fifteen minutes on Line 1. Check the bag sealer.
